title: Start or resume a unit
text: Resume this workspace. Call orientation and learning_path, read my current checkpoint and the actual unlocked sources. Teach the next useful part using this vault's preferences: clear explanation, a complete example and useful visuals. Save concise source-linked notes, offer a small focused card batch, leave a brief unanswered check and preserve my place. Do not treat prepared output as learning or unlock advanced references.

title: Continue from my checkpoint
text: Continue from my current checkpoint without repeating the whole introduction. Read the current route and source pages first. Use my actual prior answer if present; if none is present, do not invent one. Explain the next useful part and leave a clear stopping point.

title: Prepare the current part
text: Distill the current unlocked unit into a useful lesson, not a whole-book summary. Identify the essential ideas, prerequisites already needed here, important figures/tables, one complete worked example and common mistakes. Cite physical PDF pages. Flag source/OCR uncertainty, create focused notes and leave checks unanswered. Keep advanced references locked.

title: Explain a confusing point
text: Help me understand this point: {{topic}}. Read the relevant current sources. Explain the mechanism in plain language, use a concrete example and a visual if it helps. Check symbols, assumptions and important exceptions. Ask one targeted check only after the explanation; do not turn this into a long quiz.

title: Trace a mechanism visually
text: Make a visual explanation of {{topic}} within the current unit. Choose the clearest medium: labelled diagram, interactive state trace or silent animation. Ground the labels and causal steps in actual sources. For interactivity, provide pause/step/reset, clear state and edge cases; run the available validation and inspect the result. Explain how to read it and retain an editable source.

title: Make an editable concept map
text: Create a small editable Draw.io map for the current unit. Use only meaningful source-supported concepts and labelled relations. Keep labels readable and avoid crossings/overlaps. Export and inspect an image, retain the native file and link the useful concepts to my notes. A successful export is not proof the content is correct.

title: Create focused Anki cards
text: Create a small high-value card batch from the current explained unit. One retrieval target per card, clear prompts, concise answers, a short reason and an exact source locator. Use stable keys to prevent duplicates, sync through the card outbox and report actual delivery. Do not rate cards, invent reviews or create a deck from every sentence.

title: Check understanding after a unit
text: Give me a short check on the current unit after a concise reminder of its goal. Include a reasoning/application question, not just vocabulary. Wait for my answer before grading it. Record only my actual attempt and assistance level. Keep model examples, reading exposure and mastery distinct.

title: Prepare for my syllabus
text: Use my supplied syllabus and any actual past-paper examples to prioritize the current unit for exams. Repair unclear source explanations, show representative worked questions and distinguish essential concepts from low-value detail. State uncertainty if the marking scheme or exam format is unknown; do not pretend to predict the exam.

title: Explain a medical mechanism
text: Explain {{topic}} for medical study using the current assigned material. Start with normal structure/function, then trace the mechanism and connect it to relevant findings or educational investigations. Use a labelled pathway or comparison table. Verify anatomy against source figures and label simplifications. Use fictional educational examples, with source locators and a brief check.

title: Critically read a paper
text: Critically read this paper: {{paper}}. Retrieve the original text and identify its publication/preprint status and date. Explain its question, design, sample, methods, comparison, results, effect sizes and uncertainty where reported. Separate authors' claims from evidence, observational association from causation and missing information from negative results. Save a concise source-linked evidence note and tell me what this paper cannot establish.

title: Investigate a research question
text: Investigate this question: {{topic}}. Define scope, a useful question structure and search terms; use PICO only if appropriate. Search relevant primary sources, read methods/results and build a source-linked evidence table with dates, populations, designs, findings and limitations. Label preprints, conflicting evidence and uncertain coverage. Do not invent citations or call this a systematic review without the required protocol and search process.

title: Learn the highest-value coding topic
text: Teach {{topic}} as it matters to my actual projects with an agent helping me implement. Use current official documentation and repository evidence where available. Prioritize decisions I must judge: contracts, state/data flow, debugging, testing and failure modes. Show a complete small example, let the agent handle routine boilerplate and give me a brief practical check.

title: Add books without changing the syllabus
text: Import this vault's PDF inbox and show the actual registered sources, editions and page counts. Report intake/OCR errors honestly and preserve originals. Index locally, then help me place the book on a chronological learning route. Do not upload whole books, silently assign advanced prerequisites or treat possession as learning.

title: Identify my current account
text: Call codex_account_status and report this workspace's selected account, effective next slot and the account that actually served the latest completed request. Give me the actual account-control and Study setup links. Do not guess from your writing style or change any setting.

title: Use the secondary account
text: Switch this workspace to the secondary Codex account with fallback enabled, using select_codex_account. Read back the setting and distinguish the already-running request from subsequent model calls. Keep the current model and the accounts' own limits unchanged.

title: Restore automatic account selection
text: Return this workspace to automatic Codex account selection with fallback enabled. Verify the selection with codex_account_status. Do not change the model, learner memory, course progress or PDF processing preference.

title: Use Modal for OCR in this vault
text: Set this vault's PDF processing preference to Modal for future OCR/layout calls and read it back. Explain the personal admission limits and actual processing location. Do not upload any page just to test the setting; digital text and verified cached pages can remain local. Give me the setup page if authorization or deployment is missing.

title: Use local PDF processing
text: Set this vault's PDF processing preference to local and read it back. Preserve source originals, prepared pages, corrections, cards and learning progress. Do not reprocess pages merely because the backend preference changed.
